rule: Two-part names per building (prefix list x type-suffix list) drawn with a seed per building, so the same building always gets the same name; a notice board shows one common rumour under a centred town name, chosen by weight (quest rumours weighted above ambient gossip), one rumour per NPC per talk; faction reputation changes ripple to allies and enemies at half strength and down the faction tree, with the origin and root taking the full change. Donor code uses the Unity RNG in several picks and takes the first common rumour for the sign.
keep: Two-part names from a culture bank, seeded per building or zone, so the same place always reads the same.
Notice board as a centred title, a spacer and one rumour in one message box.
Weighted rumour pick with quest news outweighing ambient gossip.
One rumour per NPC per conversation.
Region-to-faction map and a parent-child faction tree with a ripple to allies and enemies.
Bank of region singleton names for landmark buildings.
change: Replace every UnityEngine.Random pick with the seeded server picker (monsters, rumours, quest variants).
Bulletin board picks by weight over the sign-filtered list instead of the first rumour.
Decide Monster3: weight it in or delete it; it is unreachable now.
Carry the remainder in the half-change ripple, so a change of 1 is not lost.
Give GetTextTokens a real variant index or a bool; it currently returns variant 0 for any value other than -1.
Add a visited set to the knightly and temple ripple branches, unverified loop risk.
Check ally and enemy lists in both directions at load.
Use our own word lists and weights; no Daggerfall names or rumour text.
look_test: Build one notice board in a starter zone with three rumour variants chosen by weight and a fixed comparator. Dom taps the board six times on a 375-wide phone. Judge whether the zone name reads as a place, whether the rumour varies, whether each line fits without a fourth line, and whether a quest rumour outranks ambient gossip often enough to notice. Style flag only; no release rows.
